# How the OpenSSL archives in this directory were built.
#
# The four committed archives are binaries, not sources, so nothing in a diff
# says where they came from. OpenSSL itself compiles its build configuration
# into libcrypto (crypto/cversion.c), so each archive carries its own version,
# target, compiler line and build date. This file records what those should be;
# ci/scripts/check-vendored-provenance.sh reads them back out of the archives
# and compares. A version bump that forgets this record goes red without anyone
# tampering with anything.
#
# Fields the check compares (per platform section): platform, compiler, built on,
# and the version -- against both the record and the directory name. It ALSO
# compares each `no-<feature>` token of the configure lines against the
# OPENSSL_NO_<FEATURE> macro it must produce in that platform's committed
# include/openssl/configuration.h, in both directions. So a configure line that
# does not describe the build under it fails, and so does a build that was given
# a flag the line does not record.
# Fields recorded but NOT measurable, and therefore not compared: source-sha256,
# signing-key, cross-signed-by, host, and the parts of a configure line that emit
# no macro at all (`no-shared`, `no-module`, the target triple, --prefix,
# --openssldir). Configure skips `module` when it writes OPENSSL_NO_* macros, so
# configuration.h is the same with and without it; what `no-module` changes is
# visible only in the archive, which then defines ossl_legacy_provider_init.
#
component: openssl
version: 3.5.8
source-url: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/releases/download/openssl-3.5.8/openssl-3.5.8.tar.gz
source-sha256: a8f84a39918ec6415ce765d9b429d313ba97b8143169c172e734b9514464f5b2
signing-key: B146647E45A7B33947AB226B2A2C87D161692D40 (primary; signed by subkey C46ED3F2CBEFDA1FDAADA44264ED7B1DCCE71CB2)
cross-signed-by: 216094DFD0CB81EF 2026-06-01 OpenSSL <openssl@openssl.org> (retired key, sig!)

host: Linux 6.12.104-1-MANJARO x86_64 GNU/Linux, gcc (GCC) 16.2.1 20260810, perl 5.42.2
config-delta: seven OPENSSL_NO_* macros are new against the 3.5.5 archive, none
config-delta: gone. Four follow from no-engine (ENGINE, AFALGENG, CAPIENG,
config-delta: PADLOCKENG); three -- APPS, DOCS, TESTS -- follow from the
config-delta: no-apps/no-docs/no-tests flags, which measurement says the 3.5.5
config-delta: archive was NOT built with: configuring 3.5.8 without those three
config-delta: flags emits none of the three macros, so their absence from the
config-delta: 3.5.5 header is evidence about that build, not about the version.
config-delta: None of the three changes library code; they only skip building
config-delta: the apps, the docs and the test suite.
platform: linux-x86_64
compiler: gcc -fPIC -pthread -m64 -Wa,--noexecstack -Wall -O3 -DOPENSSL_USE_NODELETE -DL_ENDIAN -DOPENSSL_PIC -DOPENSSL_BUILDING_OPENSSL -DNDEBUG

configure: lipo -create <x86_64-staging>/System/Library/LibreSCRS/openssl/lib/libcrypto.a <arm64-staging>/System/Library/LibreSCRS/openssl/lib/libcrypto.a -output macosx/lib/libcrypto.a
build-paths: OpenSSL compiles its install layout into libcrypto: OPENSSLDIR (openssl.cnf,
build-paths: cert.pem and certs/), MODULESDIR (provider modules) and ENGINESDIR. Built
build-paths: with --prefix=<staging> they named the build host's staging directory, a
build-paths: path inside a user's home directory that the user can write to; every
build-paths: process that created an OpenSC context on that host dlopen()ed whatever
build-paths: legacy.dylib was there, because OpenSC loads the legacy provider by name on
build-paths: every sc_context_create. Two changes close that:
build-paths:   no-module builds the legacy provider into libcrypto (providers/build.info:
build-paths:   `IF[{- $disabled{module} -}]` puts liblegacy into libcrypto with
build-paths:   STATIC_LEGACY; crypto/provider_predefined.c then lists "legacy" with its
build-paths:   init function), so loading it by name never touches the disk.
build-paths:   --prefix/--openssldir name a directory under /System/Library, which does
build-paths:   not exist and which System Integrity Protection keeps anyone, root
build-paths:   included, from creating. No configuration, trust anchors or modules are
build-paths:   read from disk through the compiled-in defaults -- the same as on every
build-paths:   user's machine before, where the build host's path did not exist either.
build-paths:   Not /System/Library/OpenSSL: that one exists and holds an openssl.cnf
build-paths:   libcrypto would load as its configuration, which can name providers to
build-paths:   load (and a certs/ directory that would become a trust-anchor source).
build-paths:   The install is staged with
build-paths:   DESTDIR, so the compiled-in paths are never created on the build host.
build-paths: Check: strings -n 8 macosx/lib/libcrypto.a | grep -E 'DIR: '
build-env: MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 (pins otool -l LC_BUILD_VERSION minos to the
build-env: project's CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET; clang honours the env var with no
build-env: -mmacosx-version-min needed on the Configure line -- unset, it defaulted to
build-env: the active SDK's own major version, 26.0, which is a newer floor than the
build-env: project targets). make was invoked as `make -j3 PLATFORM=macos-<arch>`: the
build-env: PLATFORM make variable feeds only crypto/buildinf.h's "platform: " string
build-env: (util/mkbuildinf.pl; grep '$(PLATFORM)' Makefile has exactly that one hit),
build-env: never a compiler flag or path, so the override is cosmetic and does not
build-env: change what was compiled. Without it, darwin64-<arch>-cc's stock Configure
build-env: target embeds "platform: darwin64-<arch>-cc" verbatim (util/mkbuildinf.pl
build-env: writes the raw Configure target name through) -- there is no stock OpenSSL
build-env: target literally named macos-arm64/macos-x86_64 (checked Configurations/
build-env: *.conf). The override reproduces the label the 3.5.5 archive already
build-env: carried and that this file's own [macosx] platform: lines, the gate's
build-env: macos-prefix universal check, and this component's README section all
build-env: assume; recorded here because the plain Configure line alone reproduces
build-env: neither that label nor this file's own expectation of it.
